title: Melbourne Grasses, Ferns & More
description: Grasses, sedges, rushes, ferns and other plants of Greater Melbourne.
attribution: Species lists and photos: iNaturalist contributors (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA). Text: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0).

cards.name: Austral Bracken
cards.subtitle: Pteridium esculentum
cards.description: Pteridium esculentum, commonly known as bracken fern, austral bracken or simply bracken, is a species of the bracken genus native to a number of countries in the Southern Hemisphere. Although it is now known to contain the carcinogen ptaquiloside, the rhizome of the plant was a staple in traditional Māori diets in New Zealand and was eaten by Indigenous Australians.
cards.keyFeatures: Pteridium esculentum grows from creeping rhizomes, which are covered with reddish hair. From them arise single large roughly triangular fronds, which grow to 0.5–2 metres (1 ft 8 in – 6 ft 7 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) jirau, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Kangaroo Grass
cards.subtitle: Themeda triandra
cards.description: Themeda triandra is a species of C4 perennial tussock-forming grass widespread in Africa, Australia, Asia and the Pacific. In Australia it is commonly known as kangaroo grass and in East Africa and South Africa it is known as red grass and red oat grass or as rooigras in Afrikaans. Kangaroo grass was formerly thought to be one of two species, and was named Themeda australis.
cards.keyFeatures: Themeda triandra is a perennial grass which grows in dense tufts up to 1.5 metres (5 ft) tall and 0.5 m (1+1⁄2 ft) wide. It flowers in summer, producing large red-brown spikelets on branched stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Spiny-headed Mat-rush
cards.subtitle: Lomandra longifolia
cards.description: Lomandra longifolia, commonly known as spiny-head mat-rush, spiky-headed mat-rush, or basket grass, is a perennial, rhizomatous herb found throughout eastern Australia. The leaves are 40 cm to 80 cm long, and generally have a leaf of about 8 mm to 12 mm wide. It grows in a variety of soil types and is frost, heat and drought tolerant.
cards.imageCredit: (c) James K. Douch, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by James K. Douch

cards.name: Yellow Rush-lily
cards.subtitle: Tricoryne elatior
cards.description: Tricoryne elatior (common name yellow autumn-lily, yellow rush-lily) is a species of flowering plant in the family Asphodelaceae, native to Australia, and found in all its states and territories.
cards.keyFeatures: Tricoryne elatior is a rhizomatous perennial herb, with fibrous roots, It grows to a height of 10-40 cm but sometimes grows to 1 m. The leaves are linear, 5–10 cm by 1–3.5 mm wide, and usually glabrous.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rolf Lawrenz, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rolf Lawrenz

cards.name: Yorkshire Fog
cards.subtitle: Holcus lanatus
cards.description: Holcus lanatus is a perennial flowering plant in the grass family Poaceae. The specific epithet lanatus is Latin for 'woolly' which describes the plant's hairy texture. Common names include Yorkshire fog, tufted grass, and meadow soft grass.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Orchard Grass
cards.subtitle: Dactylis glomerata
cards.description: Dactylis glomerata is a species of flowering plant in the grass family Poaceae, commonly known as barnyard grass, cocksfoot grass, cockspur, orchard grass, or cat grass (due to its popularity for use with domestic cats). It is a cool-season perennial C3 tufted grass native throughout most of Europe, temperate Asia, and northern Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: Cock's-foot grows in dense perennial tussocks to 20–140 centimetres (7.9–55.1 in; 0.66–4.59 ft) tall, with grey-green leaves 20–50 centimetres (7.9–19.7 in; 0.66–1.64 ft) long and up to 1.5 centimetres (0.59 in) broad, and a distinctive tufted triangular flowerhead 10–50 centimetres (3.9–19.7 in; 0.33–1.64 ft) long, which may be either green or red- to purple-tinged (usually green in shade, redder in full sun), turning pale grey-brown at seed maturity.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Podschwit, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Harry Podschwit

cards.name: Sweet Vernal Grass
cards.subtitle: Anthoxanthum odoratum
cards.description: Anthoxanthum odoratum is a short-lived perennial grass, commonly known as sweet vernal grass, that is native to acidic grassland in Eurasia and northern Africa. It is grown as a lawn grass and a houseplant, due to its sweet scent, and can also be found on unimproved pastures and meadows. The specific epithet odoratum is Latin for 'odorous'.
cards.keyFeatures: Anthoxanthum odaoratum is a short-lived perennial grass that grows in tufts with stems up to 70 cm (28 in) tall. The leaves are short and broad, 3–5 mm (0.12–0.20 in) wide, and glabrous to loosely hairy.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tom Norton, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tom Norton

cards.name: Rough Tree-fern
cards.subtitle: Cyathea australis
cards.description: Alsophila australis, synonym Cyathea australis, also known as the rough tree fern, is a species of tree fern native to southeastern Queensland, New South Wales and southern Victoria in Australia, as well as Tasmania and Norfolk Island. It was known as beeow-wang in Illawarra, as pooeet at Corranderrk Station in Victoria, and as nanga-nanga in Queensland.
cards.keyFeatures: The massive erect trunk is usually up to 12 m tall, although specimens reaching 20 m have been reported from Queensland, Australia. Fronds are bi- or tripinnate and may reach 4 m in length, occasionally even 6 m.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Whitington, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Whitington

cards.name: Common Maidenhair Fern
cards.subtitle: Adiantum aethiopicum
cards.description: Adiantum aethiopicum, also known as the common maidenhair fern, is a small fern of widespread distribution, occurring in Africa, Australia, Norfolk Island and New Zealand. Adiantum aethiopicum was one of the many species first described by Linnaeus, in this case in his Systema naturae in 1759.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by insiderelic

cards.name: Greater Quaking Grass
cards.subtitle: Briza maxima
cards.description: Briza maxima is a species of the grass genus Briza. It is native to Northern Africa, Western Asia and Southern Europe and is cultivated or naturalised in the British Isles, the Azores, Australasia, the western United States, Central and South America, and Hawaii.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Saryu Mae 前 朝琉, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Saryu Mae 前 朝琉

cards.name: Tall Flatsedge
cards.subtitle: Cyperus eragrostis
cards.description: Cyperus eragrostis is a species of sedge known by several common names, including tall flatsedge, nutgrass, tall nutgrass, umbrella sedge, chufa, Earth almond, zula nuts, edible galingale and pale galingale. In New Zealand, it is also known by the Māori name Puketangata. This species is associated with disturbed wet environments.
cards.keyFeatures: Cyperus eragrostis is a tufted herbaceous plant in the sedge family that is commonly mistaken for a type of grass. However, it can be differentiated from grasses by many features.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by insiderelic

cards.name: Mother Shield-fern
cards.subtitle: Polystichum proliferum
cards.description: Polystichum proliferum, commonly known as mother shield fern is an Australian endemic fern. The genus name Polystichum is derived from Greek poly - many, and stichos - rows referring to the many rows of sori. The species name is derived from Latin, Proli – offspring and fer - bearing referring to the proliferous buds, a prominent feature of the species.
cards.keyFeatures: Polystichum proliferum is a terrestrial fern that can grow to 130 cm in height. The rhizome and frond bases are covered in persistent scales which are glossy brown with pale edges.
cards.imageCredit: (c) James K. Douch, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Common Reed
cards.subtitle: Phragmites australis
cards.description: Phragmites australis, the common reed, is a species of flowering plant in the grass family Poaceae. It is a wetland grass that can grow up to 2–6 metres (7–20 ft) tall and has a cosmopolitan distribution worldwide.
cards.keyFeatures: Phragmites australis commonly forms extensive stands (known as reed beds), which can cover huge areas, an example being in the Danube Delta, where it covers 1,700 square kilometres (170,000 ha) in area. It can grow in damp ground, in standing water up to 1 m (3 ft 3 in) deep, or as a floating mat.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Wattle Mat-rush
cards.subtitle: Lomandra filiformis
cards.description: Lomandra filiformis, commonly known as wattle mat-rush, is a tussock forming perennial herb that is native to Australia. It is sparsely tufted, with strap-like leaves and yellow flowers. It grows in dry sclerophyll forest and grassy woodland, usually on well-drained rocky or sandy soils.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bat's Wing Fern
cards.subtitle: Histiopteris incisa
cards.description: Histiopteris incisa, the bat's wing fern, water fern or fern mata, is a common plant found in Australia, New Zealand and other islands in the south Pacific region. Usually found in moist areas, where it may form large colonies. The lowermost lobes of each pinnae have a bat wing like appearance, giving the fern its common name.
cards.keyFeatures: Histiopteris incisa is a medium-sized fern, usually producing fronds of approximately 60–200 cm in length. Fronds are widely spaced, distinct, and slightly dimorphic with fertile lobes slightly narrower than the infertile lobes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Caterpillar Grass
cards.subtitle: Paspalum dilatatum
cards.description: Paspalum dilatatum is a species of grass known by the common name dallisgrass, Dallas grass, or sticky heads. It is native to Brazil and Argentina, but it is known throughout the world as an introduced species and at times a common weed. Its rapid growth and spreading rhizomes make it an invasive pest in some areas.
cards.keyFeatures: This is a perennial bunch grass forming dense, stiff clumps in the soil and spreading outward. It grows decumbent in a mat or erect to well over 1 m (3 ft) tall.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Hugo Hulsberg

cards.name: Soft Tree-fern
cards.subtitle: Dicksonia antarctica
cards.description: Dicksonia antarctica, commonly known as the soft tree fern, is a species of fern native to eastern Australia, ranging from south-east Queensland to Tasmania. It is commonly grown as an ornamental both in Australia and elsewhere.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jean-Michel Moullec, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Cleavers
cards.subtitle: Galium aparine
cards.description: Galium aparine, commonly called cleavers, and also known as bedstraw, catchweed, goose grass, sticky bob, sticky willy, and velcro plant, is an annual, herbaceous plant of the family Rubiaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Cleavers are annuals with creeping straggling stems that branch and grow along the ground and over other plants. They attach themselves by the small hooked hairs that grow on the stems and leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Magnus Hagdorn, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Weeping-grass
cards.subtitle: Microlaena stipoides
cards.description: Microlaena stipoides, synonym Ehrharta stipoides, is a species of grass. It occurs naturally in all states of Australia as well as in New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the Philippines. It has also been introduced into Hawaii and Reunion Island and has been reported as invasive in both.
cards.keyFeatures: Microlaena stipoides grows to a height of approximately 0.7 metres and produces delicate, drooping stalks of spikelets. The naked caryopses (grains) are similar in shape to rice grains but smaller, approximately 5 mm long, with a mass that varies widely, ranging from 1 mg to 7 mg.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Longflower Veldtgrass
cards.subtitle: Ehrharta longiflora
cards.description: Recorded 633 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jon Sullivan

cards.name: Neat Feather-moss
cards.subtitle: Pseudoscleropodium purum
cards.description: Pseudoscleropodium purum, or neat feather-moss, is a species of moss and the sole representative of the genus Pseudoscleropodium.
cards.keyFeatures: The species is described as having a pleurocarpous growth habit that forms soft carpets or turfs. It has regularly pinnate shoots up to 15 cm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Helen Waterman, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Helen Waterman

cards.name: Cypress-leaved Plait-moss
cards.subtitle: Hypnum cupressiforme
cards.description: Hypnum cupressiforme, the cypress-leaved plaitmoss or hypnum moss, is a common and widespread species of moss belonging to the genus Hypnum. It is found in all continents except Antarctica and occurs in a wide variety of habitats and climatic zones. It typically grows on tree trunks, logs, walls, rocks and other surfaces.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas

cards.name: Blue Pigroot
cards.subtitle: Sisyrinchium micranthum
cards.description: Sisyrinchium micranthum, commonly known as annual blue-eyed grass, blue pigroot, fairy stars, and striped rush-leaf, is a wildflower. It is a grass-like species in the iris family, Iridaceae. It is native to Mexico, Central America, and South America and widely naturalized elsewhere.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Kangaroo Fern
cards.subtitle: Microsorum pustulatum
cards.description: Zealandia pustulata is a species of fern native to eastern Australia and New Zealand. It is commonly referred to as 'kangaroo fern' or 'kangaroo paw fern' as its native range includes Australia and the shape of its mature foliage tends to resemble the shape of a kangaroo's foot. It is also referred to as 'hound's tongue', and as kōwaowao and pāraharaha in the Māori language.
cards.keyFeatures: This epiphytic fern species seems to climb onto suitable substrates (fallen logs, rocks, growing plants etc.) via long, creeping grey-green rhizomes. The rhizomes have clathrate, ovate scales which are 3-7 mm long and 1-2 mm wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Katja Schulz, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Katja Schulz

cards.name: Screw Fern
cards.subtitle: Lindsaea linearis
cards.description: Lindsaea linearis is known as the screw fern, as the fronds may have a twisting appearance. It has a creeping stem with fronds that can grow up to 50 cm (20 in) in length. It is a small fern of widespread distribution in many parts of Australia, as well as New Zealand and New Caledonia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leon Perrie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Leon Perrie

cards.name: Kikuyu Grass
cards.subtitle: Cenchrus clandestinus
cards.description: The tropical grass species Cenchrus clandestinus (previously Pennisetum clandestinum) is known by several common names, most often Kikuyu grass. It is native to the highland regions of East Africa that is home to the Kikuyu people. Because of its rapid growth and aggressive nature, it is categorised as a noxious weed in some regions.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Thatch Saw-sedge
cards.subtitle: Gahnia radula
cards.description: Gahnia radula, commonly known as the thatch saw-sedge is a tufted perennial sedge native to south-eastern Australia. The leaves are long, flat and rough, with sharp edges. It has a distinctive brown inflorescence, which darkens to black.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Forest Wire-grass
cards.subtitle: Tetrarrhena juncea
cards.description: Recorded 504 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Juniper Haircap Moss
cards.subtitle: Polytrichum juniperinum
cards.description: Polytrichum juniperinum, commonly known as juniper haircap or juniper polytrichum moss, is an evergreen and perennial species of moss that is widely distributed, growing on every continent including Antarctica.
cards.keyFeatures: The stems are reddish with grey-green leaves that have a distinctive red-brown tip. This characteristic allows them to be separated from the bristly haircap (Polytrichum piliferum), a plant that the juniper haircap moss closely resembles.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Krauss's Clubmoss
cards.subtitle: Selaginella kraussiana
cards.description: Selaginella kraussiana is a species of vascular plant in the family Selaginellaceae. It is referred to by the common names Krauss' spikemoss, Krauss's clubmoss, or African clubmoss, and is found naturally in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa and in Macaronesia.
cards.keyFeatures: Growing to just 5 cm (2.0 in) high, it is a low-growing, mat-forming evergreen perennial with primitive fern-like leaves, that spreads via rooting stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Panic Veldtgrass
cards.subtitle: Ehrharta erecta
cards.description: Ehrharta erecta is a species of grass commonly known as panic veldtgrass. The species is native to Southern Africa and Yemen. It is a documented invasive species in the United States, New Zealand, Australia, southern Europe and China.
cards.imageCredit: (c) strewick, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by strewick

cards.name: Quill Moss
cards.subtitle: Cyathophorum bulbosum
cards.description: Cyathophorum bulbosum, commonly known as quill moss or the false fern moss, is found in the eastern states of Australia (QLD, NSW, VIC, TAS and south-eastern SA) as well as Papua New Guinea, New Zealand, Auckland Islands, Chatham Island, Lord Howe Island and possibly Norfolk Island and New Ireland.
cards.keyFeatures: Cyathophorum bulbosum is often mistaken for a small fern due to its appearance. The stem can grow up to 20 cm, although is generally found around the 5–15 cm range, with the longer specimens found in Tasmania and Victoria.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leon Perrie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Leon Perrie

cards.name: Knobby Clubrush
cards.subtitle: Ficinia nodosa
cards.description: Ficinia nodosa, the knotted club-rush or knobby club-rush, is a rhizomatous perennial in the family Cyperaceae, native to South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand. Widespread in the Southern Hemisphere, Ficinia nodosa grows to between 15 and 220 cm in height. Although it grows best in sandy, salty soil, the plant grows in a wide variety of environments from coastal sand dunes to alpine regions.
cards.keyFeatures: Ficinia nodosa, a grass-like sedge, grows to roughly 100 centimetres (39 in) in height, with its smooth, green-yellow stems spreading up to 200 centimetres (79 in) in diameter. The stems themselves grow to between 15 and 100 centimetres (5.9 and 39.4 in) in length and 1 to 2 millimetres (0.039 to 0.079 in) in diameter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Michael Berardozzi, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Michael Berardozzi

cards.name: Prairie Grass
cards.subtitle: Bromus catharticus
cards.description: Bromus catharticus is a species of brome grass known by the common names rescue grass (America), prairie grass (New Zealand), and Schrader's bromegrass in English, and cebadilla criolla and cebadilla in Spanish. It is the most common and most well-known of several species in the Bromus catharticus complex within the Bromus section Ceratochloa, all of which are hexaploids with the chromosome count 2n=42.
cards.keyFeatures: Bromus catharticus is a coarse winter annual or biennial grass, growing 0.2–1 m (7.9 in – 3 ft 3.4 in) in height. The culms of the grass are glabrous and 2–4 mm (0.079–0.157 in) thick.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paúl Gonzáles, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paúl Gonzáles

cards.name: Broom Spurge
cards.subtitle: Amperea xiphoclada
cards.description: Ampera xiphloclada, commonly known as ‘broom spurge’, is a grass-like erect shrub in the Euphorbiaceae family.
cards.keyFeatures: The smooth relatively thin branched, erect shrub is often lime green with dull, light brown sessile clustered flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Whitington, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Whitington

cards.name: Grass Triggerplant
cards.subtitle: Stylidium graminifolium
cards.description: Stylidium graminifolium, the grass triggerplant, is a dicotyledonous plant that belongs to the genus Stylidium (family Stylidiaceae). This species used to belong to the Stylidium graminifolium complex, but the name was conserved for this single species when two others were split from the complex and introduced as new species in 2001.
cards.keyFeatures: This species is an erect perennial herb with 5–40 cm (2–8 in) long narrow, grass-like leaves that appear from a basal rosette. A 15–90 cm (6–36 in) long scape bearing the racemous inflorescence appears in the spring and summer (October through February).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Vale Jenny Conolly

cards.name: Pale Grass Lily
cards.subtitle: Caesia parviflora
cards.description: Caesia parviflora, the pale grass lily, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asphodelaceae, subfamily Hemerocallidoideae, native to Australia, being found in New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria, Tasmania, South Australia and Western Australia. This is a small plant up to 50 centimeters tall, found in heath, woodland and dry sclerophyll forest, usually near grasses. It often grows on sandstone-based soils.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Petra Holland, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Petra Holland

cards.name: Chilean Needle Grass
cards.subtitle: Nassella neesiana
cards.description: Recorded 393 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Fishbone Water-fern
cards.subtitle: Blechnum nudum
cards.description: Lomaria nuda, commonly known as the fishbone waterfern, is a fern that grows up to a metre tall, and is abundant in rainforest and eucalyptus forests in eastern Australia. The species is placed in the genus Lomaria in the Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification of 2016 (PPG I), but is often retained in genus Blechnum as Blechnum nudum.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Tall Sword-sedge
cards.subtitle: Lepidosperma elatius
cards.description: Lepidosperma elatius is a species of plant from the sedge family that can be found in Australia (in New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland and Tasmania). The plant grows to a height of 1–2.5 metres (3 ft 3 in – 8 ft 2 in), with leaves 5–15 millimetres (0.20–0.59 in) in width, and which are convex on both sides, with sharp margins. The spikelets have a drooping spray with a length of 18–65 centimetres (7.1–25.6 in).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Black Windmill Grass
cards.subtitle: Chloris truncata
cards.description: Chloris truncata, known by the common names Australian fingergrass, windmill-grass, Australian windmill grass and simply windmill grass locally in Australia, is a perennial grass. Chloris truncata is a low-growing grass forming a small clump of around 30 centimetres in diameter. It has long leaves, approximately 10–15 cm long with a distinctive blunt tip and flattened leaf sheath at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Miguel de Salas, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Miguel de Salas

cards.name: Red-anther Wallaby Grass
cards.subtitle: Rytidosperma pallidum
cards.description: Rytidosperma pallidum (syn. Joycea pallida), commonly known as red-anther wallaby grass, is an Australian species of tussock grass found in Victoria, New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. The grass has flowers in December, and the flowers have a prominent red anther, after which it is commonly named.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Heath Star-moss
cards.subtitle: Campylopus introflexus
cards.description: Campylopus introflexus, also known as the heath star moss, is a species of moss. The first description of the species was made by the German botanist Johannes Hedwig as Dicranum introflexum in 1801.
cards.keyFeatures: Individual plants measure 0.5–5 centimetres (0.2–2.0 in), with lanceolate leaves 4–6 mm (0.16–0.24 in). The costa is wide and occupies about half the leaf width.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Justin Paulin, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Justin Paulin

cards.name: Tall Sedge
cards.subtitle: Carex appressa
cards.description: Carex appressa, the tall sedge, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cyperaceae. It is native to New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and generally in the South West Pacific.
cards.keyFeatures: Carex appressa is a densely tufted, perennial sedge that forms clumps up to 50 cm (20 in) in diameter. Its stems grow to around 100 cm (39 in) in height, and are hard and solid, becoming rough towards the top of the stem.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Colin Meurk, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Colin Meurk

cards.name: Little Quaking-grass
cards.subtitle: Briza minor
cards.description: Briza minor is a species of grass known by the common names lesser quaking-grass or little quakinggrass. It is native to the Mediterranean Basin, and it is known elsewhere, including much of North America, as an introduced species. It is an annual grass producing narrow clumps of erect stems up to 50 centimeters tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ken-ichi Ueda, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Red-fruit Saw-sedge
cards.subtitle: Gahnia sieberiana
cards.description: Gahnia sieberiana, commonly known as the red-fruit saw-sedge, is a tussock-forming perennial plant in the family Cyperaceae, endemic to Australia. It is a widespread plant that favours damp sunny sites. Many insect larvae have been recorded feeding on the red-fruit saw-sedge.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lucas Christofides, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lucas Christofides

cards.name: Shaking Brake
cards.subtitle: Pteris tremula
cards.description: Pteris tremula, commonly known as Australian brake, tender brake, tender brakefern, shaking brake is a fern species of the family Pteridaceae native to sheltered areas and forests in eastern Australia and New Zealand. It has pale green, lacy fronds of up to 2 meters (6.6 feet) in length. It is fast-growing and easy to grow in cultivation, but can become weedy.
cards.keyFeatures: Pteris tremula is a terrestrial fern, with its fronds arising from the ground up to 1.3 m (4.3 ft) with an erect, tufted rhizome that is covered with narrow brown scales, rarely up to 2 m (6.6 ft) tall. The stipe is brown.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Ecroyd, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Ecroyd

cards.name: Queensland Blue Grass
cards.subtitle: Dichanthium sericeum
cards.description: Recorded 260 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blue Grass Lily
cards.subtitle: Caesia calliantha
cards.description: Caesia calliantha, commonly known as the blue grass lily or blue star lily, is a species of herbaceous flowering plant. It is a member of the Asphodelaceae family, subfamily Hemerocallidoideae, native to Australia found predominantly along the East coast in Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia and Tasmania.
cards.keyFeatures: Caesia calliantha is a tufted, perennial plant from the family Asphodelaceae. It has fibrous roots with broad spindle and tubers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Beach Spinifex
cards.subtitle: Spinifex sericeus
cards.description: Spinifex sericeus, commonly known as hairy spinifex, rolling spinifex, beach spinifex or coastal spinifex, is a dioecious perennial grass. It is native to Australia, New Zealand, New Caledonia, and Tonga. It is an important pioneer species which colonises coastal dunes, binding loose sand with its horizontal runners.
cards.keyFeatures: Spinifex sericeus has branched stolons and rhizomes extending up to 1–2 metres (3.3–6.6 ft). The leaves have a ligule of a rim of dense hairs; the blades are flat and densely silky.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bruce Calvert, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bruce Calvert

cards.name: Gristle Fern
cards.subtitle: Oceaniopteris cartilaginea
cards.description: Oceaniopteris cartilaginea, synonym Blechnum cartilagineum, is known as the gristle fern or soft water fern. It is a resilient and abundant fern growing in eastern Australia, seen in rainforest and eucalyptus forest. The new growth is often pink or reddish in colour.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Greg Tasney, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Greg Tasney

cards.name: Hard Water-fern
cards.subtitle: Blechnum wattsii
cards.description: Parablechnum wattsii, synonym Blechnum wattsii, is a common terrestrial fern growing in rainforest and open forest. It is often seen near creeks in much of south eastern Australia, including Victoria, Tasmania (and King Island), South Australia, New South Wales and Queensland. The specific epithet wattsii honours William Walter Watts (1856-1920).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bryce Watts-Parker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Winter Grass
cards.subtitle: Poa annua
cards.description: Poa annua, or annual meadow grass (known in America more commonly as annual bluegrass or simply poa), is a widespread low-growing turfgrass in temperate climates. Notwithstanding the reference to annual plant in its name, perennial biotypes do exist. It originated as an allopolyploid hybrid between Poa supina and Poa infirma.
cards.keyFeatures: It has a slightly creeping, fibrous rootstock. The stem grows from 15–25 cm (6–10 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) James K. Douch, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Many Flowered Matrush
cards.subtitle: Lomandra multiflora
cards.description: Lomandra multiflora, also commonly known as many-flowered mat rush, mat rush and many flowered mat-lily, is a perennial, rhizomatous herb found in Australia and Papua New Guinea. The mat rush is distributed widely in the region and common within its preferred growing conditions. Its conservation status is considered not to be of concern and risk.
cards.keyFeatures: Lomandra multiflora, commonly known as many-flowered mat-rush, mat rush or many-flowered mat-lily is a tufted perennial, rhizomatous herb native to Australia. Lomandra multiflora is part of the Lomandra genus with around 50 species, all of which are native to Australia and generally share common characteristics.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lorraine Phelan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lorraine Phelan

cards.name: Red Azolla
cards.subtitle: Azolla rubra
cards.description: Azolla rubra, known commonly as red azolla and Pacific azolla, is a species of aquatic fern native to Australia and New Zealand. In New Zealand, it is also known by its Māori names returetu, roturotu, kārearea and kārerarera.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Katie Jenkins, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Katie Jenkins

cards.name: Couch
cards.subtitle: Cynodon dactylon
cards.description: Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a warm season grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates. It is native to Europe, Africa, Australia, and much of Asia and has been introduced to the Americas. Despite its common name, C. dactylon is not native to Bermuda but is an abundant invasive species there.
cards.keyFeatures: The blades are grey-green in color and short, usually 2–15 cm (0.79–5.91 in) long with rough edges. The erect stems can grow 1–30 cm (0.39–11.81 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Phalaris
cards.subtitle: Phalaris aquatica
cards.description: Phalaris aquatica, known by the common names bulbous canary-grass and Harding grass, is a species of grass in the genus Phalaris of the family Poaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an erect, waist-high, stout perennial bunch grass, with grayish to bluish green leaves. Flowering heads are dense, spike-like, and usually 2 to 5 inches (50 to 125 mm) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Serrated Tussock
cards.subtitle: Nassella trichotoma
cards.description: Nassella trichotoma, commonly known as the serrated tussock, is a type of bunchgrass plant, native in Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, and Peru. It is on the list of Weeds of National Significance in Australia, reducing the productivity of pasture and creating a fire hazard. In many states, landowners are required by law to keep their land free of this plant.
cards.keyFeatures: Nassella trichotoma tends to grow cespitose (in dense tufts), and stands about 20 cm (7.9 inches) to 60 cm (24 inches) tall. The branches usually grow between two and 6 cm (2.4 inches) long, and the caryopses (simple fruits) grow around 1.2 mm (0.047 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Josh

cards.name: Pipe-cleaner Moss
cards.subtitle: Ptychomnion aciculare
cards.description: Ptychomnion aciculare (colloquially known as ‘Pipe-cleaner Moss’) is a species of moss found predominantly in Australia, New Zealand, New Caledonia, Samoa, Juan Fernandez Islands and Chile. It is easily recognised given its similarity, especially when partially dried, to a pipe-cleaner. This name is commonly accepted across Australia and New Zealand.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Steve Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Steve Kerr

cards.name: Common Pampas Grass
cards.subtitle: Cortaderia selloana
cards.description: Cortaderia selloana is a species of flowering plant in the family Poaceae. It is referred to by the common name pampas grass, and is native to southern South America, including the Pampas region after which it is named. It is widely distributed throughout the world as a cultivated ornamental and invasive species.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Fernando de Gorocica, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Hedgehog Grass
cards.subtitle: Echinopogon ovatus
cards.description: Echinopogon ovatus, or hedgehog grass, is a species of grass. It is indigenous to Australia and New Zealand. It has bluish-green tufts which grow up to around 140 cm (55 in).
cards.keyFeatures: Echinopogon ovatus is a lax, tufted grass up to 140 cm (55 in) tall. The culm is upright-decumbent, baring an ovate panicle made up of 20–30 green spikelets with finely scabrid awns.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Great Brome
cards.subtitle: Bromus diandrus
cards.description: Bromus diandrus is a species of grass known by the common names great brome and "ripgut brome".
cards.keyFeatures: This is a brome grass which is native to the Mediterranean but has been introduced to much of the rest of the world. It does best in areas with a Mediterranean climate, such as California and parts of southern Australia, but it is quite tolerant of many climates.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Ben Keen

cards.name: Hare's Tail Grass
cards.subtitle: Lagurus ovatus
cards.description: Lagurus is a genus of Old World plants in the grass family, native to the Mediterranean Basin and nearby regions, from Madeira and the Canary Islands to Crimea and Saudi Arabia. It is also naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, the Azores, Ireland and Great Britain, and scattered locations in the Americas. The only known species is Lagurus ovatus, commonly called hare's-tail, hare's-tail grass or bunnytail.
cards.keyFeatures: Lagurus ovatus is a clump-forming annual growing to 50 cm (20 in) tall by 30 cm (12 in) tall, with pale green grassy foliage and numerous short, oval green flowerheads, turning to a buff colour as they ripen, all summer long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Arnim Littek, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Arnim Littek

cards.name: Long Hair Plume Grass
cards.subtitle: Pentapogon crinitus
cards.description: Recorded 201 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Barkla, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by John Barkla

cards.name: Feathered Mosquito Fern
cards.subtitle: Azolla pinnata
cards.description: Azolla pinnata is a species of fern known by several common names, including mosquitofern, feathered mosquitofern and water velvet. It is native to much of Africa, Asia (Brunei Darussalam, China, India, Japan, Korea, and the Philippines) and parts of Australia. It is an aquatic plant, it is found floating upon the surface of the water.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Auradyme, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Auradyme

cards.name: River Tussock Grass
cards.subtitle: Poa labillardierei
cards.description: Poa labillardierei, also known as common tussock-grass, is a species of tussock grass that is endemic to Australia. It is found in southern and eastern Australia, including Tasmania. There are differing variations, Poa labillardierei var. acris Vickery and Poa labillardierei var. labillardierei.
cards.keyFeatures: Poa labillardierei is a dense coarsely tufted grasses and can reach a height of 120 cm. The large grass is a perennial, that germinates from seed or division.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Great Soft-rush
cards.subtitle: Juncus pallidus
cards.description: Juncus pallidus, commonly known as the great soft-rush pale rush, giant rush, or leafless rush is a species of rush that is native to southern Australia, New Zealand, Norfolk Island, and Lord Howe Island. It is a vigorous, tufted, tussock-forming, rhizomatous perennial herb with culms growing to 70–135 cm in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Whitington, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Whitington

cards.name: Soft Brome
cards.subtitle: Bromus hordeaceus
cards.description: Bromus hordeaceus, the soft brome, is an annual or biennial species of grass in the grass family (Poaceae). It is also known in North America as bull grass, soft cheat, and soft chess. It is the most common species of Bromus in Britain, where it can be found on roadsides, waste ground, meadows, and cultivated land.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is pubescent entirely and lacks rhizomes. It can grow 7–110 cm (3–43 in) high, sometimes in tufts, sometimes singly.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Wolfgang Jauch, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Wolfgang Jauch

cards.name: Veined Bristle-fern
cards.subtitle: Trichomanes venosum
cards.description: Polyphlebium venosum, the veined bristle-fern or bristle filmy fern, is a fern in the family Hymenophyllaceae. It is only found in wet forests, mainly growing as an epiphyte on the shady side of the soft tree fern, Dicksonia antarctica. It also grows on logs, trunks of trees and rarely on trunks of Cyathea species or on wet rock-faces.
cards.keyFeatures: The sporophyte stage has rhizome branched and creeping, very fine, densely covered with tiny, pale brown hairs. Fronds well spaced, pendent, 5–15 cm long, delicate and translucent; stipe and rachis thread-like.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Tassel Sedge
cards.subtitle: Carex fascicularis
cards.description: Carex fascicularis, commonly known as tassel sedge, is a species of sedge of the family Cyperaceae that is native to Australia, New Zealand and New Guinea.
cards.keyFeatures: The monoecious and rhizomatous perennial grass-like sedge has a tufted habit and typically grows to a height of 0.6 to 1.5 metres (2 to 5 ft). and a width of 0.5 to 0.75 m (1 ft 8 in to 2 ft 6 in).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Tassel Rope-rush
cards.subtitle: Hypolaena fastigiata
cards.description: Hypolaena fastigiata, commonly known as tassel rope-rush or bundled rope rush, is a plant species in the family Restionaceae. It is endemic to Australia, and commonly found in sandy-soil habitats. It is distinctive among other species in Hypolaena due to ascending culms with a round cross section, glaucous colour when young, glabrous when mature, and very small fruit dangling creating a tassal like appearance.
cards.keyFeatures: Hypolaena fastigiata is a perennial, diecious herb that spreads from rhizomes, forming diffuse patches up to 2m across. Arising from the rhizomes are culms that are usually straight to sinuous or flexuosa, 20-60 cm long and can be very branched.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Feather Speargrass
cards.subtitle: Austrostipa elegantissima
cards.description: Austrostipa elegantissima, commonly known as tall feather-grass, is a species of grass in the family Poaceae. It is native to southern Australia, from Western Australia to New South Wales. It grows as a decumbent perennial in a rhizomatous tussock with widespread leaves, and lacks basal leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Common Nardoo
cards.subtitle: Marsilea drummondii
cards.description: Marsilea drummondii is a species of fern known by the common name nardoo (Diyari: ngardu). It is native to Australia, where it is widespread and common, particularly in inland regions. It is a rhizomatous perennial aquatic fern that roots in mud substrates and produces herbage that floats on the surface of quiet water bodies.
cards.imageCredit: (c) ian_mcallan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blown Grass
cards.subtitle: Lachnagrostis filiformis
cards.description: Lachnagrostis filiformis (syn. Agrostis avenacea) is a species of grass known by the common names Pacific bent grass, New Zealand wind grass, fairy grass, or blown-grass.
cards.keyFeatures: Pacific bent grass is a tufted perennial grass growing up to 65 centimeters tall. The leaf blades are flat and about 8-25 centimeters long and 2-3 millimeters wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Cloak Fern
cards.subtitle: Cheilanthes sieberi
cards.description: Cheilanthes sieberi is a small fern growing in many parts of Australia, New Zealand and nearby islands. Common names include poison rock fern and mulga fern. This fern may grow up to 25 centimetres (10 inches) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Third Silence, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Third Silence

cards.name: Common Wood-rush
cards.subtitle: Luzula meridionalis
cards.description: Recorded 163 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Parramatta Grass
cards.subtitle: Sporobolus africanus
cards.description: Sporobolus africanus, or rat's tail grass, is a true grass in the tribe Zoysieae.
cards.keyFeatures: Sporobolus africanus is an erect, stiff, tufted, perennial grass. Leaves are 20–40cm long and 1–4mm wide, in-rolled, scabrid, and olive-green.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Ecroyd, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Ecroyd

cards.name: Clustered Wallaby-grass
cards.subtitle: Rytidosperma racemosum
cards.description: Rytidosperma racemosum or wallaby grass, is a species of grass endemic to eastern Australia, but naturalised in New Zealand, Hawaii (USA), and California (USA). It was described as Danthonia racemosa in 1810 by Scottish botanist Robert Brown. Two varieties are recognized: Rytidosperma racemosum var. racemosum Rytidosperma racemosum var. obtusatum
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Rock Fern
cards.subtitle: Cheilanthes austrotenuifolia
cards.description: Cheilanthes austrotenuifolia is a species of Australian rock fern from the family Pteridaceae. Once a common understory plant along streams in moist areas of Southern Australia, Cheilianthes austrotenuifolia is still quite widespread in remnant bush-land, such as areas of the Adelaide Hills, although it has been affected significantly by land clearance and competition from invasive species.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by insiderelic

cards.name: Tall Spike-rush
cards.subtitle: Eleocharis sphacelata
cards.description: Eleocharis sphacelata, commonly known as tall spikerush, is a sedge of the family Cyperaceae that is native to Australia and New Zealand. The erect rhizomatous perennial herb to grass-like sedge typically grows to a height of 1 to 2 metres (3.3 to 6.6 ft). It blooms between February and October producing white flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Giant Moss
cards.subtitle: Dawsonia superba
cards.description: Dawsonia superba is a moss in the family Polytrichaceae that is found in Australia, New Guinea, Malaysia, and New Zealand. D. superba is the tallest self-supporting moss in the world, reaching heights of 60 cm (24 in).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Soft-stem Bulrush
cards.subtitle: Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani
cards.description: Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani is a species of flowering plant in the sedge family known by the common names grey club-rush, softstem bulrush, and great bulrush.
cards.keyFeatures: Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani is quite variable in appearance, thus explaining the long list of synonyms that have been created over the years. It is a perennial herb producing dense stands of many narrow erect stems reaching 1–1.5 m (3–5 ft), rarely to 3 m (10 ft), in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Patrick Hacker, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Patrick Hacker

cards.name: Australian Salt-grass
cards.subtitle: Distichlis distichophylla
cards.description: Distichlis distichophylla is a species of grass commonly known as Australian salt-grass, emu grass or pineapple grass. It is a dioecious perennial plant that grows to about 30 cm in height, with creeping rhizomes up to 1 m long. It is coarse and prickly, growing in damp, saline areas such as the fringes of saltmarshes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Yoav Daniel Bar-Ness, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Yoav Daniel Bar-Ness

cards.name: Necklace Fern
cards.subtitle: Asplenium flabellifolium
cards.description: Recorded 135 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.keyFeatures: The fronds are 10 to 20 cm (3.9 to 7.9 in) long, with 5 to 20 pairs of pinnae (leaflets), often fan-shaped or sometimes lanceolate. The fronds are flaccid and tend to droop.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Heather Merrylees, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Heather Merrylees

cards.name: Blue Wheat Grass
cards.subtitle: Anthosachne scabra
cards.description: Anthosachne scabra is a species of true grass of the tribe Triticeae. This species is found in New Zealand and Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: A. scabra is an open, hairy grass with long drooping inflorescences with more-or-less straight awned spikelets. Its branching can be intravaginal and extravaginal.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alice Shanks, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alice Shanks

cards.name: Mother Spleenwort
cards.subtitle: Asplenium gracillimum
cards.description: Asplenium gracillimum is a fern species native to Australia and New Zealand, also found in Stewart Island and the Chatham Islands. The specific epithet gracillimum refers to the slender and graceful appearance of this fern.
cards.keyFeatures: A. gracillimum individuals occasionally grow small bulbils on top of their fronds, which can fall off and grow into new ferns. There are a number of similar Southern Hemisphere species which have a similar mode of reproduction, including A. daucifolium and Polystichum australiense.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Katja Schulz, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Katja Schulz

cards.name: Common Ground Fern
cards.subtitle: Calochlaena dubia
cards.description: Calochlaena dubia, commonly known as soft bracken, false bracken, common ground fern or rainbow fern, is a small Australian fern in the treefern family Dicksoniaceae. It is very common within its range, and often seen growing under eucalyptus forest, often on the poorer quality soils. It is an easy plant to grow in the garden.
cards.keyFeatures: The fronds arise from the thick brown haired rhizomes and are anywhere from 0.4 to 1.5 m in height. The foliage is a more yellow green colour, in contrast to the darker shiny green of bracken (Pteridium esculentum).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sam Westbrook, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Sam Westbrook

cards.name: Barnyardgrass
cards.subtitle: Echinochloa crus-galli
cards.description: Echinochloa crus-galli is a species of wild grass originating from tropical Asia that was formerly classified as a panicum grass. It is commonly known as cockspur, cockspur grass, barnyard grass, barnyard millet, water grass, cocksfoot grass, cockshin grass. It is sometimes referred to using the general term, barnyard grass, which may refer to any species of the genus Echinochloa.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Carter Dorscht

cards.name: Rabbitfoot Grass
cards.subtitle: Polypogon monspeliensis
cards.description: Polypogon monspeliensis, commonly known as annual beard-grass or annual rabbitsfoot grass, is a species of grass. It is native to the Old World, but it can be found today throughout the world as an introduced species and sometimes a noxious weed. It is an annual grass growing to heights between 5 centimeters and one meter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Matt Lavin, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Slender Pigeon-grass
cards.subtitle: Setaria parviflora
cards.description: Setaria parviflora is a species of grass known by the common names marsh bristlegrass, knotroot bristle-grass, bristly foxtail and yellow bristlegrass. It is native to North America, including Mexico and the United States from California to the East Coast, Central America and the West Indies, and South America. This grass is a perennial with small, knotty rhizomes.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Variable Sword-sedge
cards.subtitle: Lepidosperma laterale
cards.description: Lepidosperma laterale, commonly known as the variable swordsedge, is a plant found in south-eastern Australia, New Caledonia, and New Zealand. It is often found on sandy soils or rocky areas in wooded areas. The specific epithet laterale is derived from the Latin, which refers to the sides.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jenny Christianson

cards.name: Long Smoothcap
cards.subtitle: Atrichum androgynum
cards.description: Recorded 112 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Three-spiked Goose Grass
cards.subtitle: Eleusine tristachya
cards.description: Recorded 111 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacob Moore, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Selliera
cards.subtitle: Goodenia radicans
cards.description: Goodenia radicans, commonly known as remuremu, swampweed, bonking grass, or its former botanical name Selliera radicans, is a creeping, herbaceous plant species found in New Zealand, Australia and Chile. It is the most observed Goodenia on iNaturalist in New Zealand, and is indigenous to New Zealand and Australia. Only one other Goodenia is native to New Zealand, the severely range-restricted Goodenia heenanii.
cards.keyFeatures: A low-lying herb with short green leaves, which forms matted patches. It bears small white flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Swamp Spikemoss
cards.subtitle: Selaginella uliginosa
cards.description: Selaginella uliginosa is a small plant in the spikemoss family Selaginellaceae which is endemic to Australia. An ancient and primitive plant, usually under 10 centimetres tall, it is often seen in sunny moist areas. The specific epithet uliginosa is from Latin, referring to the plant's preference for growing in swampy locations.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jean-Paul Boerekamps

cards.name: Kneed Wallaby-grass
cards.subtitle: Rytidosperma geniculatum
cards.description: Recorded 106 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Michael D. Pirie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Michael D. Pirie

cards.name: Bristly Wallaby-grass
cards.subtitle: Rytidosperma setaceum
cards.description: Rytidosperma setaceum, known by various common names including small-flowered wallaby-grass, mulga- or bristly wallaby-grass, is a species of grass native to Australia. Originally described by Robert Brown under the name Danthonia setacea, it was transferred into Austrodanthonia by Hans Peter Linder in 1993 and finally Rytidosperma in 2011. From the earlier name, setacea means bristle or stiff hair.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Pennyroyal
cards.subtitle: Mentha pulegium
cards.description: Mentha pulegium, commonly (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. Crushed pennyroyal leaves emit a very strong fragrance similar to spearmint.
cards.keyFeatures: An annual to perennial plant with creeping or erect branched stems to about 40 cm in height. The stems are square in cross-section and can vary from hairless on some plants to densely hairy on others, with a green to sometimes red or purplish colour.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Wendy F, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Soft Water-fern
cards.subtitle: Blechnum minus
cards.description: Parablechnum minus, synonym Blechnum minus, is a small fern growing in moist situations in a variety of habitats in eastern Australia. It is often seen by streams. It first appeared in scientific literature in the year 1810, as Stegania minor in the Prodromus Florae Novae Hollandiae, published by the prolific Scottish botanist, Robert Brown.
cards.imageCredit: (c) naturewatchwidow, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by naturewatchwidow

cards.name: Golden Weather-grass
cards.subtitle: Hypoxis hygrometrica
cards.description: Hypoxis hygrometrica, known as the golden weather-grass, is a small herbaceous plant. It is found in south eastern Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Petra Holland, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Petra Holland

cards.name: Spiny Rush
cards.subtitle: Juncus acutus
cards.description: Juncus acutus, the spiny rush, sharp rush or sharp-pointed rush, is a flowering plant in the monocot family Juncaceae. It is native to the Americas, Northern and Southern Africa, Western and Southern Europe and West Asia, and is found in a variety of wet habitats, such as bogs, fens, meadows, and salt marshes, and along the edges of ponds and lakes.
cards.keyFeatures: Juncus acutus is a brown and green tussock-forming perennial that can grow to 1.5 metres (4.9 ft) tall in all kinds of soils, in areas which go from extremes in flood and dry like dunes or that just stay wet like lowland grassland and grassy woodland, riparian vegetation, freshwater wetland, and saline and subsaline wetlands.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Red-heart Moss
cards.subtitle: Breutelia affinis
cards.description: Recorded 97 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Colin Meurk, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Colin Meurk

cards.name: Veined Spear-grass
cards.subtitle: Austrostipa rudis
cards.description: Recorded 97 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Wall Barley
cards.subtitle: Hordeum murinum
cards.description: Hordeum murinum is a species of flowering plant in the grass family Poaceae, commonly known as wall barley or false barley. It is a close relative of cultivated barley (H. vulgare).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Karim Haddad, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Karim Haddad

cards.name: Fountain Grass
cards.subtitle: Cenchrus setaceus
cards.description: Cenchrus setaceus, commonly known as crimson fountaingrass, is a C4 perennial bunch grass that is native to open, scrubby habitats in East Africa, tropical Africa, the Middle East and south-western Asia. It has been introduced to many parts of the world as an ornamental plant, and has become an invasive species in some of them.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Grey Sedge
cards.subtitle: Carex divulsa
cards.description: Carex divulsa, the grey sedge, is a species of flowering plant in the genus Carex, native to Macaronesia, Europe, northwest Africa, the Caucasus region, and the Middle East as far east as Turkmenistan. It has been introduced to northeast Argentina, the District of Columbia and Pennsylvania in the United States, Ontario in Canada, the North Island of New Zealand, and Tasmania and Victoria in Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Soft Speargrass
cards.subtitle: Austrostipa mollis
cards.description: Austrostipa mollis, also known as the soft speargrass or supple speargrass, is a robust, erect tufted perennial speargrass in the Poaceae family. It is native to Australia, and found in Western Australia, South Australia, Victoria, ACT and Tasmania. It was first described as Stipa mollis by Robert Brown in 1810 from a specimen collected in Tasmania.
cards.keyFeatures: A perennial erect, robust and tufted grass to 1.4 m tall. Stem nodes have downy hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Red Grass
cards.subtitle: Bothriochloa macra
cards.description: Bothriochloa macra, commonly known as red-leg grass, red grass, redleg or pitted beard grass is a perennial grass species that is native to eastern Australia and New Zealand. It is naturalised in Tasmania and Norfolk Island.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Faccenda, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kevin Faccenda

cards.name: Knot Grass
cards.subtitle: Paspalum distichum
cards.description: Paspalum distichum is a species of grass. Common names include knotgrass, water finger-grass, couch paspalum, eternity grass, gingergrass, and Thompson grass. Its native range is obscure because it has long been present on most continents, and in most areas it is certainly an introduced species.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Robert McPherson, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Coast Speargrass
cards.subtitle: Austrostipa stipoides
cards.description: Austrostipa stipoides, commonly known as prickly spear-grass or coast spear-grass, is a kind of tussock grass native to the coasts of south-eastern Australia and of New Zealand. It forms large clumps up to about 80 cm in height with smooth inrolled leaves 70 cm long and 1 mm wide with sharp tips. It is found on sea cliffs, the edges of beach dunes and salt marshes and tolerates strong winds and sea spray.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Harry Rose

cards.name: Scarlet Kammetjie
cards.subtitle: Freesia laxa
cards.description: Freesia laxa, commonly known as flowering grass, is a small species of cormous flowering plant in the family Iridaceae, from eastern and southern Africa, from Kenya to northeastern South Africa. It is grown in gardens as an ornamental plant.
cards.keyFeatures: Freesia laxa grows from corms, reaching about 15–30 cm (6–12 in) tall. The green leaves are arranged in a flat "fan" from which the flower stalk emerges.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dr. Alexey Yakovlev, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Dr. Alexey Yakovlev

cards.name: Sparse Fern Moss
cards.subtitle: Thuidiopsis sparsa
cards.description: Thuidiopsis sparsa is a species of moss in the family Thuidiaceae. The natural distribution includes Australia, Papua New Guinea, New Zealand and nearby islands.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Scrambling Coral-fern
cards.subtitle: Gleichenia microphylla
cards.description: Gleichenia microphylla is a small fern growing in Australia and New Zealand. Some of the other common names include: scrambling coral fern, umbrella fern, parasol fern, carrier tangle, matua-rarauhe, matuku, tapuwae kotuku, waewae kaka, waewae kotuku and waewae matuku. A common plant, often seen growing under waterfalls, in swamps, under cliffs and in tall open forest.
cards.keyFeatures: Gleichenia microphylla's rachis on major branches has conspicuous and numerous bundles of bristles that are shiny, short, and amber to dark brown in colour. It also has less numerous and scattered fringed scales.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Katie Jenkins, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Katie Jenkins

cards.name: Poongort
cards.subtitle: Carex tereticaulis
cards.description: Carex tereticaulis, also known as basket sedge, is a species of sedge of the family Cyperaceae that is native to southern parts of Western Australia, southern parts of South Australia, southern and eastern parts of New South Wales as well as north western and central Victoria and Tasmania. The Koori peoples know the plant as Poong'ort.
cards.keyFeatures: The monoecious and rhizomatous perennial grass-like sedge has a tufted habit and typically grows to a height of 0.7 to 1.2 metres (2.3 to 3.9 ft). It blooms between September and October or November producing brown flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terra Occ

cards.name: King Fern
cards.subtitle: Todea barbara
cards.description: Todea barbara, known as the king fern or crape fern, is a fern in the family Osmundaceae occurring in moist areas of south eastern Australia, and also indigenous to New Zealand, Australia and South Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: The king fern grows up to 3 metres (10 ft) tall, but has a short stumpy base. The fronds are up to 2.5 metres (8.2 ft) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) magriet b, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by magriet b

cards.name: Perennial Ryegrass
cards.subtitle: Lolium perenne
cards.description: Lolium perenne, common name perennial ryegrass, English ryegrass, winter ryegrass, or ray grass, is a grass from the family Poaceae. It is native to Europe, Asia and northern Africa, but is widely cultivated and naturalised around the world.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is a low-growing, tufted and hairless grass, with a bunching (or tillering) growth habit. The leaves are dark green, smooth and glossy on the lower surface, with untoothed parallel sides and prominent parallel veins on the upper surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Георгий Виноградов (Georgy Vinogradov), some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Георгий Виноградов (Georgy Vinogradov)

cards.name: Common Spike-rush
cards.subtitle: Eleocharis acuta
cards.description: Eleocharis acuta, commonly known as common spikerush or small spikerush, is a sedge of the family Cyperaceae that is native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The rhizomatous perennial herb to grass-like sedge typically grows to a height of 0.7 metres (2.3 ft). It blooms between September and December producing brown flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lisa Bennett, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lisa Bennett

cards.name: Bonfire Moss
cards.subtitle: Funaria hygrometrica
cards.description: Funaria hygrometrica, the bonfire moss or common cord-moss, is a type of water moss which grows on shady, moist soil. It can also be found on moist walls and the crevices of rocks and places where recent fires have taken place. It has been reported to grow in Niagara Cave, an artificially illuminated cave devoid of natural light.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Igor Balashov, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Igor Balashov

cards.name: Annual Ryegrass
cards.subtitle: Lolium rigidum
cards.description: Lolium rigidum is a species of annual grass. Common names by which it is known include annual ryegrass, a name also given to Italian ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum), rigid ryegrass, stiff darnel, Swiss ryegrass and Wimmera ryegrass.
cards.keyFeatures: Lolium rigidum is an annual grass that grows in open tussocks. It has fibrous roots and can grow up to a metre tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Christian Berg, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Christian Berg

cards.name: Smilo Grass
cards.subtitle: Oloptum miliaceum
cards.description: Oloptum miliaceum is a species of grass known by the common name smilograss. It is native to Eurasia but it can be found in many other parts of the world as an introduced species and a casual weed of disturbed areas. It is a clumping perennial grass producing sturdy, erect stems that can reach 1.5 meters tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Matt Lavin, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Buffalo Grass
cards.subtitle: Stenotaphrum secundatum
cards.description: St. Augustine grass (Stenotaphrum secundatum), also known as buffalo turf in Australia and buffalo grass in South Africa, is a species of grass in the family Poaceae. It is a warm-season lawn grass that is popular for cultivation in tropical and subtropical regions.
cards.keyFeatures: St. Augustine is a dark green grass with broad, flat blades.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Common Bog-rush
cards.subtitle: Schoenus apogon
cards.description: Schoenus apogon, known as common bog-rush, is a species of sedge native to eastern Australia, New Zealand and Japan. A tufted annual grass-like plant growing to 55 cm tall. Often seen in seasonally wet habitats.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Slender Wild Oat
cards.subtitle: Avena barbata
cards.description: Avena barbata is a species of wild oat known by the common name slender wild oat. It has edible seeds. It is a diploidized autotetraploid grass (2n=4x=28).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jesse Rorabaugh

cards.name: Pouched Coral Fern
cards.subtitle: Gleichenia dicarpa
cards.description: Gleichenia dicarpa, commonly known as pouched coral fern or tangle fern, is a small fern of the family Gleicheniaceae found in eastern Australia, New Caledonia and New Zealand. It can also be found in parts of Southeast Asia. It forms tangled thickets in wet places such as swamps and riverbanks.
cards.keyFeatures: G. dicarpa consists of numerous fronds arising more or less vertically from a thin many branched rhizome. Each frond can reach 2 m (7 ft) in length with pinnae up to 4 cm (1.6 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Mark, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Mark

cards.name: Common Filmy-fern
cards.subtitle: Hymenophyllum cupressiforme
cards.description: Hymenophyllum cupressiforme is a southern hemisphere species of filmy fern. Found in moist sheltered areas, in or near rainforests. Occasionally found in drier protected areas.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Blady Grass
cards.subtitle: Imperata cylindrica
cards.description: Imperata cylindrica (commonly known as cogongrass or kunai grass ) is a species of perennial rhizomatous grass native to tropical and subtropical Asia, Micronesia, Melanesia, Australia, Africa, and Southern Europe. It has also been introduced to Latin America, the Caribbean, and the Southeastern United States.
cards.keyFeatures: Cogongrass grows from 0.2–3 m (1⁄2–10 ft) tall, its stalk is firm and has nodes covered with long white hairs. Each clump that grows shares an extensive rhizome network, the biomass of which accounts for 60% of the total biomass of the plant.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Fern-grass
cards.subtitle: Catapodium rigidum
cards.description: Catapodium rigidum, ferngrass, is a species of annual grass in the family Poaceae (true grasses), distributed around the Mediterranean and the Middle East. It has been widely introduced throughout drier parts of the world, including parts of North America, South America, South Africa, Korea, Australia, and New Zealand. Individuals can reach 20 cm (8 in).
cards.keyFeatures: Fern-grass can be difficult to distinguish from sea fern-grass in places where they occur together, but it has a more open panicle and the stalk to the inflorescence is ridged, whereas it is rounded on one side in sea fern-grass.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alex Whitesides, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alex Whitesides

cards.name: Long Forkfern
cards.subtitle: Tmesipteris obliqua
cards.description: Tmesipteris obliqua, more commonly known as the long fork-fern or common fork-fern, is a weeping, epiphytic fern ally with narrow unbranched leafy stems. T. obliqua is a member of the genus Tmesipteris, commonly known as hanging fork-ferns. Tmesipteris is one of two genera in the order Psilotales, the other genus being Psilotum.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Perennial Veldtgrass
cards.subtitle: Ehrharta calycina
cards.description: Ehrharta calycina is a species of grass known by the common names perennial veldtgrass and purple veldtgrass.
cards.keyFeatures: Ehrharta calycina is a highly variable perennial grass, often but not always rhizomatous. It usually reaches 30–70 centimetres (12–28 in) in height, but is known to grow much taller in favorable conditions.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Common Leaf-rush
cards.subtitle: Cyperus lucidus
cards.description: Cyperus lucidus is a species of sedge that is native to Australia and New Guinea. The species was first formally described by the botanist Robert Brown in 1810.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Copper-awned Wallaby Grass
cards.subtitle: Rytidosperma fulvum
cards.description: Recorded 68 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nina Kerr

cards.name: Hairy Crabgrass
cards.subtitle: Digitaria sanguinalis
cards.description: Digitaria sanguinalis is a species of grass known by several common names, including hairy crabgrass, hairy finger-grass, large crabgrass, crab finger grass, purple crabgrass. It is one of the better-known species of the genus Digitaria, and one that is known nearly worldwide as a common weed.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an annual grass with an inflorescence of up to nine very long, very thin, radiating branches atop its stems. Each branch is lined with pairs of very tiny spikelets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Gyselinck, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Gyselinck

cards.name: Shiny Filmy-fern
cards.subtitle: Hymenophyllum flabellatum
cards.description: Hymenophyllum flabellatum (Hymen-O-FIL-lum Flab-bel-Lah-tum), the shiny filmy-fern, is a species of fern in the family Hymenophyllaceae. This delicate fern is commonly epiphytic and is between 5 and 25 cm in length. It is distinct, with its thin, one-celled thick, membranous leaves.
cards.keyFeatures: The filmy-fern is distinct by its thin, one cell thick, membranous fronds, that grow in moist areas. Fronds are pale yellow green, covered in yellow-brown hairs, and 5–25 cm in length.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Hugo Innes, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Knob Sedge
cards.subtitle: Carex inversa
cards.description: Carex inversa, commonly known as knob sedge, is a species of sedge of the family Cyperaceae that is native to parts of Australia and New Zealand and has also been introduced into Great Britain.
cards.keyFeatures: The monoecious and rhizomatous perennial grass-like sedge has a tufted habit and typically grows to a height of 0.3 to 0.75 metres (1 to 2 ft). It blooms between September and October producing brown flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ben Fisher, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blanket Fern
cards.subtitle: Asplenium subglandulosum
cards.description: Recorded 62 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Giant Mountain Grass
cards.subtitle: Dryopoa dives
cards.description: Dryopoa, or giant mountain grass, is a genus of Australian plants in the grass family. The only known species is Dryopoa dives, native to New South Wales, Tasmania, and Victoria. The name Dryopoa (tree-grass) is derived from the Greek language, with dryos meaning tree and poa meaning grass.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Bearded Screwmoss
cards.subtitle: Pseudocrossidium crinitum
cards.description: Recorded 60 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Toad Rush
cards.subtitle: Juncus bufonius
cards.description: Juncus bufonius, known commonly as toad rush, is a widespread flowering plant species complex in the rush family Juncaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Juncus bufonius is an annual monocot that is quite variable in appearance. It is generally a green clumping grasslike rush, with many thin stems wrapped with few threadlike leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Mehdi Chetibi, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Mehdi Chetibi

cards.name: Meadow Foxtail
cards.subtitle: Alopecurus pratensis
cards.description: Alopecurus pratensis, known as the meadow foxtail or the field meadow foxtail, is a perennial grass belonging to the grass family (Poaceae). It is native to Europe and Asia. It is a common plant is found on grasslands, especially on neutral soils.
cards.keyFeatures: It flowers from April until June – one of the earliest grasses to do so. Any survey work carried out in mid-summer may miss the grass as a result of this.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kai Löhr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kai Löhr

cards.name: Coast Sword-sedge
cards.subtitle: Lepidosperma gladiatum
cards.description: Lepidosperma gladiatum is commonly known as the coast sword-sedge or coastal sword-sedge. It is an evergreen species of sedge that is native to southern coastal areas of Australia. It was described by French botanist Jacques Labillardière in 1805.
cards.keyFeatures: L. gladiatum occurs mostly as a dense sedge that favours dunes and creek lines. Described as clump-forming perennial with stout vertical rhizome.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Clarke

cards.name: Rough Speargrass
cards.subtitle: Austrostipa scabra
cards.description: Austrostipa scabra (formerly stipa scabra) known as speargrass, is a widespread species of tussock grass found in southern and central Australia. Speargrass stems may reach 15 centimetres (5.9 in) tall, with stems up to 60 centimetres (2.0 ft) tall. There are two subspecies, scabra and falcata.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Leafy Twig-rush
cards.subtitle: Cladium procerum
cards.description: Cladium procerum, known commonly as the leafy twigrush, is a species of flowering plant in the sedge family. It is found mostly in swampland and on the margins of lakes. It grows up to 2.5 m (8 ft 2 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Field Garlic
cards.subtitle: Allium vineale
cards.description: Allium vineale (wild garlic, onion grass, crow garlic or stag's garlic) is a perennial, bulb-forming species of wild onion, native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and the Middle East. The species was introduced in Australia and North America, where it has become an invasive species.
cards.keyFeatures: All parts of the plant have a strong garlic smell. The underground bulb is 1–2 cm (0.4–0.8 in) diameter, with a fibrous outer layer.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jason Sturner, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Soft Tussock-grass
cards.subtitle: Poa morrisii
cards.description: Poa morrisii, commonly known as soft tussock-grass is a species of tussock grass that is endemic to Australia. The species was formally described in 1970 by Australian botanist Joyce Winifred Vickery based on plant material collected in Sandringham, Victoria by P. Morris in 1939.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ben Fisher, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ben Fisher

cards.name: Tassel Cord-rush
cards.subtitle: Baloskion tetraphyllum
cards.description: Baloskion tetraphyllum, commonly known as tassel rope-rush, is a species of grass native to Australia. It is a large and somewhat common species of restionaceae which can be easily identified by its bright green colour and its tasseled branches with soft, hairlike texture.
cards.keyFeatures: Baloskion tetraphyllum is an understory species which grows between 0.5-2m tall. It is a semi-erect perennial herb with rigid emergent stems (or culms) which, through repeated branching, reduces in internal rigidity causing the plant to droop along the end of its stem.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by John Tann

cards.name: Lance Water-fern
cards.subtitle: Blechnum chambersii
cards.description: Austroblechnum lanceolatum, synonym Blechnum chambersii, is a species of fern within the family Blechnaceae, found in Australia, New Zealand, Samoa and Fiji. It is indigenous to Australia and New Zealand. A. lanceolatum is commonly called lance water fern, and in New Zealand it is also referred to by its Māori names, nini and rereti.
cards.keyFeatures: A medium-sized fern with tufted fronds 85-700mm in length. The fronds are strongly dimorphic with differing sterile and fertile fronds.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Armitage, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ian Armitage

cards.name: Rough Dog's-tail
cards.subtitle: Falona echinata
cards.description: Recorded 52 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tim Messick, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tim Messick

cards.name: Silver Hairgrass
cards.subtitle: Aira caryophyllea
cards.description: Aira caryophyllea is a species of grass known by the common name silver hairgrass. It's a species of bunchgrass that is native to Europe, Africa, and Asia. It has been introduced to other continents, including North America, where it is naturalized and common.
cards.imageCredit: (c) botanygirl, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by botanygirl

cards.name: Silvery Bryum
cards.subtitle: Bryum argenteum
cards.description: Bryum argenteum (common names: silver moss, silver-green moss, silvery thread moss) is a species of moss in the family Bryaceae. It is one of the most widely recognised mosses in the world and one of the most common in urban environments, identifiable without a microscope by its characteristic silvery-white sheen when dry. The species name comes from the Latin argenteum, meaning silver.
